name: VexCL
listed_description: A C++ vector expression template library for OpenCL/CUDA.
reason: No published numbers reachable. README, docs/index.rst and docs/talks.rst contain no comparison. examples/benchmark.cpp (VexCL vs Boost.Compute sort and scan, keys/sec), examples/thrust-sort.cpp (vex::sort vs thrust::sort, 16M ints, 10 timed passes) and examples/fft_benchmark.cpp (FFTW, clFFT, cuFFT) are benchmark programs only, with no result tables in the repo and no hardware or flags stated. Issues list (benchmark-related #38, #123, #150, #210) shows no timings. Peer-reviewed papers do compare it but are blocked here (EGRESS_BLOCKED / ENOTFOUND for arxiv.org, ar5iv, epubs.siam.org, hgpu.org, academia.edu, emergentmind.com): Parallel Processing Letters sort and scan comparison, arXiv 1601.03144 (VexCL 1.3.1 vs Boost.Compute, Thrust, CUB, Modern GPU, CLOGS, Bolt on AMD R9 270, NVIDIA GTX 480 and K40), and Demidov, Ahnert, Rupp, Gottschling, SIAM J. Sci. Comput. 35(5) C453, arXiv 1212.6326 (VexCL vs Thrust, ViennaCL, MTL4 on ODE integration). WebSearch snippet of 1601.03144 only: VexCL best of the OpenCL libraries for scan below about 2M elements on the R9 270, but below 20% of CUB throughput at the largest sizes, so not a win over CUB. Paper-access retier lead (tier B, domain numerics-and-science / GPU computing, not thread-pools-work-stealing); needs the actual tables before any record.

name: vfs-pipe
listed_description: One-header library to expose internal C variables as a virtual filesystem for live inspection and tuning.
reason: Directional claim, no numbers. README (plain file README, 4 commits, 6 stars, MIT) says only 'zero-latency communication' and 'High Performance: reads/writes happen directly in your program's memory'. test.c, test2.c and test.sh contain no timing code. It is a FUSE-backed variable exporter and no comparison against sysctl, environment variables or any other baseline exists anywhere in the repo.

name: Windows Template Library
listed_description: A C++ library for developing Windows applications and UI components.
reason: No numbers. SourceForge project page (CPL 1.0 / MS-PL, last update 2026-04-13) has no benchmark or comparison against MFC or anything else; the only speed-adjacent text is a 2015 user review calling it 'extremely lightweight'. WTL is a Windows UI wrapper over ATL, not a performance library, and its category guess (filesystems-and-io) does not fit.

name: xtd
listed_description: Modern C++20 framework to create console (CLI), forms (GUI) and unit tests (xUnit) applications on Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, Android, FreeBSD and Haiku.
reason: No numbers. README (1.2k stars, MIT) has no benchmark or performance comparison; the only performance text is that it is 'written in efficient, modern C++20/23'. tests/ holds only unit_tests, manual_tests and tests directories for xtd.core, xtd.drawing, xtd.forms and xtd.tunit, no benchmarks. WebSearch for xtd benchmarks found nothing. It is a GUI/console application framework, not a filesystems-and-io library.
